subject: Post-call: NovaAI POC — integration scope, auth, and retry/idempotency plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@novaai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T10:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: NovaAI POC — integration scope, auth, and retry/idempotency plan

Hi Samira — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can scope the POC and technical onboarding: 

1) Goal & success criteria
- POC goal: integrate Redwood hosted inference for embedding + reranker pipeline and validate 90th percentile latency under target throughput.
- Success: embeddings produced in correct vector format, reranker score delta matches baseline on sample set, and graceful handling of peak bursts (no >2% 429s after mitigations).

2) Integration surface (what we'll deliver)
- SDK quickstart (Python + Node) for calls to text/embeddings/rerank endpoints (we'll include structured output for tool-calling later).
- Example batching and KV cache settings for embeddings to reduce token cost.
- Auth options: API key initially; recommendation to move to OIDC token exchange for Dedicated or SSO when you onboard.

3) Rate limits & retries (we need your input)
- Typical Redwood hosted baseline: soft quota and 429 when burst exceeds tenant throttle — recommended client pattern is exponential backoff with jitter and idempotency keys for non-idempotent operations.
- Ask: can you confirm expected steady QPS and expected peak burst concurrency (requests/min or concurrent connections)?

4) Routing & fallbacks
- Default: route to Redwood hosted model (fastest). Optional: route to your Dedicated pool for sensitive data or guaranteed capacity. We can do policy-based routing in our SDK (region, cost, SLA).

5) Structured output & tool-calling
- For the reranker + structured outputs, we'd like to know if you plan to use tool-calling (external knowledge) or a deterministic schema; that affects retry semantics for streaming responses.

Next steps
- I'll follow up with a scoped POC plan and a short checklist for SDK/instrumentation (request IDs, idempotency header examples, recommended backoff algorithm).
- Can you share peak concurrency estimates and whether your security team needs SOC2/HIPAA articulation before we start?

Attachments: poc-scope-outline.pdf (POC timeline + milestones)

Thanks — Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@novaai.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: NovaAI POC — integration scope, auth, and retry/idempotency plan

Hi Jonas — great meeting, thanks. Answers inline below and a couple of attachments from our side.

- Steady QPS: ~12 requests/sec for embeddings (we batch to 32). Peak day bursts: up to ~60 requests/sec sustained for 5–10 minutes during indexing.
- Concurrency: our ingestion workers peak at ~25 concurrent connections.
- Auth: procurement prefers OIDC/SAML for Dedicated, but for POC we can start with API keys scoped to a test project. We do rotate keys every 30 days.
- Tool-calling / structured output: we plan to use structured JSON output for the reranker (schema-driven). We'll call an internal ranking service from our pipeline — not external tool-calls during generation.
- Security: attached is the basic security questionnaire — they want SOC2 + encryption details.

Attachments: novaai-security-questionnaire.xlsx

Would like the SDK quickstart and recommended request id/idempotency guidance by early next week. Procurement loop: CC'd procure@novaai.com — they will need an initial T&C overview.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Director of Search & Relevance, NovaAI
samira@novaai.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T08:20:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: NovaAI POC — integration scope, auth, and retry/idempotency plan

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Samira's reply. Key technical asks and proposed implementation notes below; please review and suggest edits before I reply with the SDK snippet and POC checklist.

Samira's numbers: steady 12 qps (batched), peak 60 qps, 25 concurrent workers. They rotate API keys every 30 days and want OIDC for Dedicated later. They will use structured JSON for reranker (no live tool-calling).

Proposed approach (high-level):
- SDK instrumentation
  - Add an X-Request-ID header for every client call (guid v4). For non-idempotent operations (streaming responses / modify operations) require an additional Idempotency-Key header when clients retry.
  - Provide sample middleware for automatic request-id generation + logging hook that maps to Redwood trace_id.

- Retry/backoff policy
  - On 429: exponential backoff (base 300ms) with full jitter, capped at 10s; attempt up to 6 retries by default.
  - On connection error/timeouts: linear retry for 2 attempts then backoff.
  - For batched embeddings: recommend client-side batch size limits (32 items) and a per-call timeout to avoid long-running blocked requests.

- Idempotency guidance
  - For multi-step workflows (upload -> embed -> rerank), use durable request IDs so that retrying after a partial success isn't duplicated (server will return an operation idempotency token).
  - We'll publish an endpoint that accepts Idempotency-Key and returns 409 if duplicate conflicting request detected.

- Routing/fallbacks
  - Default to host (fastest) with a policy to route to Dedicated when request has header X-Dedicated: true or when tenant enters guaranteed mode.
  - Add a client-side fallback to lower-fidelity model variant when latency budget is exceeded (optional).

Action items for us:
- Karthik: prepare SDK snippet (Python) showing header insertion, retry/backoff middleware, and an example embedding batch call. Attach as sdk-instrumentation-snippet.patch.
- Marissa: start a commercial note for a provisional commitment estimate given their steady/peak numbers and OIDC transition. I'll reply to Samira with the POC checklist and the snippet by Monday EOD.

Quoted for context:

Thanks, Jonas
